additions.title: We got COVID before GTA 6
additions.blurb: The WHO called COVID-19 a pandemic on 11 March 2020. It also helped cause a global chip shortage that made cars, consoles and graphics cards hard to buy. The WHO ended the global emergency on 5 May 2023.
additions.image_license: Public domain (CDC / Alissa Eckert, MS; Dan Higgins, MAM)
additions.image_alt: CDC illustration of the coronavirus that causes COVID-19: a grey sphere covered in red spike proteins
additions.image_note: CDC Public Health Image Library illustration #23312, via Wikimedia Commons; staged as new-assets/covid-pandemic.png
additions.impact: The whole world: lockdowns, closed schools and workplaces, and a chip shortage that hit cars, consoles and graphics cards.
additions.source_note: WHO, 11 March 2020: 'We have therefore made the assessment that COVID-19 can be characterized as a pandemic.' WHO, 5 May 2023: COVID-19 'no longer constitutes a public health emergency of international concern (PHEIC)'. Chip-shortage link from the merged chip-shortage record (Wikipedia, secondary).
